chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from al-'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them (peace be upon them both)
Regarding the child who is called to give testimony, he said: 'If he reaches maturity/intellect until he realizes that it is true, his testimony is valid.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a child's testimony to be valid in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the validity of a child's testimony (*shahada*) hinges on *'aql* (intellectual maturity) rather than mere age, allowing for early discernment of truth. In Shia jurisprudence, this principle underscores the flexibility of legal capacity, linking the admissibility of evidence directly to the witness's cognitive ability to comprehend the reality of the event.
